- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.33), particularly if recent prices are trending downward; adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below recent high if sentiment was strong.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, reduce by 5–10% per day to correct for delayed correction.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment history shows 3+ negative sentiment days in last 7 days.
- Avoid overconfidence in sentiment-driven forecasts: if sentiment is >0.75 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overestimation.
